story.title: Wildfires Cause Severe Air Pollution in Southeast Asia
story.summary: Thick smoke from months of wildfires in Indonesia has led to dramatic orange skies in Palangkaraya and significant air quality issues in Singapore, where landmarks like Marina Bay Sands are obscured. The ongoing crisis highlights the severe impact of the wildfires on air pollution across Southeast Asia.

explore_lenses.label: Why does the haze pose an immediate health risk?
explore_lenses.title: Fine-particle exposure can alter daily activity
explore_lenses.summary: The cross-border haze is not only a visibility problem: Singapore’s air-quality agencies are treating it as a public-health event, particularly for people with respiratory or heart conditions. Official regional monitoring on October 15 reported air quality from unhealthy to hazardous in affected areas.

claims.text: Singapore’s National Environment Agency reported that monitoring stations in Kalimantan, Peninsular Malaysia, Singapore, Sumatra and western Sarawak recorded air quality ranging from Unhealthy to Hazardous on October 15.

NEA’s health guidance says people with chronic lung or heart disease should avoid prolonged or strenuous outdoor exertion when the 24-hour PSI is Unhealthy; children, pregnant women and older people are advised to minimise it.
Singapore’s government has convened its 28-agency Haze Task Force and says its next response tier is intended especially to protect vulnerable groups if pollution worsens.

explore_lenses.label: How did smoke spread across borders?
explore_lenses.title: Dry conditions and winds are carrying haze
explore_lenses.summary: Regional monitoring attributes the current episode to a combination of fire hotspots, persistent dry weather and winds that transport smoke across national boundaries. Peatland fire is a longstanding aggravating factor because drained peat can burn below ground and generate dense smoke.

claims.text: NEA said on October 9 that increased hotspots in southern and central Sumatra, together with unfavorable wind conditions, had worsened haze; it expected southeasterly to southwesterly winds to continue carrying smoke from southern Sumatra and Kalimantan toward Singapore.
Indonesia’s meteorological agency listed haze/smoke conditions in Menteng, Palangkaraya, on October 15, with winds reported from the south.
ASEAN identifies drained and poorly managed peatlands as especially fire-prone; peat fires can burn underground, are difficult to suppress, and produce thick haze.

ASEAN’s framework treats transboundary haze from land and forest fires as a shared regional problem requiring national prevention plus international cooperation, rather than a pollution issue confined to the fire location.

explore_lenses.label: What happens next as dry weather continues?
explore_lenses.title: Rain may help locally, but severe haze risk remains
explore_lenses.summary: The near-term outlook depends on rainfall, new hotspot activity and shifting winds. Singapore’s environmental agency expects some showers in parts of the region but warns that dry areas could continue to generate elevated haze and cross-border impacts.

claims.text: Forecast: NEA said on October 15 that dry weather was expected to persist over much of southern ASEAN, while showers were forecast in parts of Peninsular Malaysia, northern Sumatra and Borneo; it said the hotspot and haze situation was likely to remain elevated where dry conditions persist.
Forecast: NEA previously warned that Singapore’s 24-hour PSI could exceed 200, entering the Very Unhealthy range, if the haze situation deteriorated.

ASEAN’s Transboundary Haze Pollution Agreement provides for monitoring, prevention, information exchange, technical cooperation and mutual assistance among member states responding to land and forest-fire haze.

story_report.summary: Smoke from wildfires in Indonesia has turned skies orange in Palangkaraya and reduced visibility in Singapore, where Marina Bay Sands was nearly obscured. The haze has developed into a regional air-pollution crisis: Singapore’s National Environment Agency said monitoring stations across Kalimantan, Peninsular Malaysia, Singapore, Sumatra and western Sarawak recorded conditions from Unhealthy to Hazardous on October 15.

sections.heading: Health Risks From Regional Haze
sections.body: NEA advises people with chronic lung or heart disease to avoid prolonged or strenuous outdoor exertion when the 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index is Unhealthy. Children, pregnant women and older people are advised to minimise such activity. Singapore has convened its 28-agency Haze Task Force, and says a higher response tier would be aimed particularly at protecting vulnerable groups if pollution worsens.

sections.heading: Winds Spread Smoke Across Borders
sections.body: NEA said increased hotspots in southern and central Sumatra, combined with unfavorable winds, had worsened the haze. It expected southeasterly to southwesterly winds to carry smoke from southern Sumatra and Kalimantan toward Singapore, while Indonesia’s meteorological agency recorded haze or smoke in Menteng, Palangkaraya, on October 15, with winds from the south. ASEAN regards transboundary haze from land and forest fires as a regional problem requiring domestic prevention and international cooperation.

sections.heading: Dry Weather Raises Continued Haze Risk
sections.body: NEA forecast that dry weather would persist over much of southern ASEAN, although showers were expected in parts of Peninsular Malaysia, northern Sumatra and Borneo. It said hotspot and haze conditions were likely to remain elevated where dry conditions continue, and had previously warned Singapore’s 24-hour PSI could exceed 200, in the Very Unhealthy range, if conditions deteriorated. ASEAN’s haze agreement provides for monitoring, prevention, information-sharing, technical cooperation and mutual assistance.

unresolved.text: Available footage and regional monitoring do not establish pollution exposure levels for every neighbourhood or individual.
The consulted sources do not attribute smoke visible over each affected city to specific fires.
Changes in rainfall and wind direction leave the event’s duration and peak pollution level uncertain.

related_stories.summary: On October 15, hundreds of protesters marched through Bangkok to oppose the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank. Demonstrators expressed concerns about the impacts of capitalism and the policies of these financial institutions.

related_stories.title: Ukraine Resumes Strikes on Russian Oil Refineries Following Truce Breakdown
related_stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that Ukraine will resume attacks on Russian oil refineries, declaring an end to a temporary ceasefire.
